# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five (volume 2) to forty-seven (volume 4)  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v4 c5 P1](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0001), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- **Rank:** Upper-class gentlewoman / Landowner  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>; Mrs. Stephen Irving  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 c7 P29](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0029)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>; Mother Lavendar  <sub>[v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Lavendar is a tiny, dainty woman with an almost girlish face, rosy cheeks, and dimples. She has thick, snow-white hair worn in soft, becoming puffs and coils. Her large, wistful brown eyes have wood-brown tones with golden glints, and she possesses a sweet, musical voice. She prefers youthful, delicate dresses adorned with frills, laces, and ribbons, such as her favorite forget-me-not organdy.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P82](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0082), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009), [v2 c27 P19](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0019)_

## Personality

Miss Lavendar is imaginative, romantic, and deeply affectionate, possessing an enduring youthful spirit. She admits to being somewhat stubborn, proud, and prone to sulking when hurt or angry. Despite years of loneliness, she retains a humorous, optimistic nature and loves hospitality, pretend games, and company. She possesses a deep capacity for maternal tenderness and is warmly sympathetic to kindred spirits.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P65](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0065), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c23 P33](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0033), [v2 c27 P31](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0031)_

## Goals

- To preserve youthfulness and romance in her everyday existence  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P64](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0064)</sub>
- To reunite with her estranged lover, Stephen Irving  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c28 P49](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0049)</sub>

## History

Miss Lavendar Lewis spent most of her life living in a secluded, ivy-covered stone house called Echo Lodge in Grafton. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but the engagement was broken off after a trivial quarrel which her pride and sulkiness prevented her from mending. She subsequently lived for twenty-five years in isolation, maintaining her spirits through imagination, play-acting, and the companionship of her maid, Charlotta the Fourth. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discovered her home by accident and became close friends with her. Later, Anne introduced Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to her. Learning through Paul's letters that Miss Lavendar was still unmarried, Stephen Irving returned to Prince Edward Island. The two reconciled, were married in her old-fashioned garden, and departed for a new home in Boston, intending to return to Echo Lodge for their summers.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c28 P29](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0029), [v2 c28 P36](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0036), [v2 c29 P5](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0005), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because he loved the scent associated with her mother  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Engaged as a girl to Stephen Irving before a foolish quarrel broke their betrothal  <sub>[v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Lived for decades as a secluded spinster in a secluded stone house in Grafton  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c22 P0](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0000)</sub>
- Employed a succession of young handmaidens named Charlotta  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

> What is the use of being an independent old maid if you can't be silly when you want to, and when it doesn't hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>

> A broken heart in real life isn't half as dreadful as it is in books. It's a good deal like a bad tooth... > The rose is the flower of love—the world has acclaimed it so for centuries. The pink roses are love hopeful and expectant—the white roses are love dead or forsaken—but the red roses... love triumphant and perfect.  <sub>[v4 c38 P7](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0007)</sub>
